questions.question: Why do production audio generators compress raw waveforms into codec tokens before modeling them?
options: Because codec tokens make audio louder and easier to hear
Because raw audio is too long a sequence, while codecs reduce it to a much lower-rate token stream a model can handle
Because transformers cannot work on any continuous-valued signal
Because codec tokens eliminate the need for decoding back to waveform
questions.explanation: The lesson starts by noting that a five-second clip can contain 80k-240k samples, which is too long to model directly with a transformer. Neural codecs like Encodec or DAC compress audio to roughly 50-75 Hz token streams, making generation tractable.

questions.question: Which property makes speech generation a better fit for token-autoregressive models than music generation?
options: Speech has stronger local phonetic structure and benefits from causal, streaming generation
Speech contains more frequency bands than music
Speech never needs conditioning on text
Speech can only be represented with spectrogram pixels
questions.explanation: The doc says token-AR still dominates speech because speech is naturally causal and streams well. It also describes clean speech as narrow-band with strong phonetic structure, which makes next-token prediction especially effective.

questions.question: In the lesson, what does residual vector quantization (RVQ) do inside a neural audio codec?
options: It mixes the left and right stereo channels into one waveform
It converts each timestep representation into a cascade of codebook indices across multiple quantizer layers
It turns text prompts into mel spectrograms
It removes all reconstruction error after the first codebook
questions.explanation: The codec section explains that the encoder produces per-timestep vectors, then RVQ maps each vector through multiple codebooks. Each layer quantizes the residual left by the previous one, which is why errors in early layers can propagate.

questions.question: What is the core difference between the two main generative paradigms described for audio generation?
options: Token-AR predicts codec tokens sequentially, while latent diffusion or flow matching generates continuous or categorical latents by iterative denoising/transport
Token-AR only works for speech, while diffusion only works for sound effects
Token-AR operates on raw waveforms, while diffusion operates only on text embeddings
There is no practical difference; both always use the same sampling procedure
questions.explanation: The lesson contrasts decoder-only transformers over flattened codec tokens with latent diffusion or flow-matching models over audio latents. It highlights that flow matching is gaining ground for music because it samples faster and produces cleaner clips, while AR remains better for streaming speech.

questions.question: According to the production note, when should you prefer the codec autoregressive path over flow-matching audio models?
options: When you need the absolute smallest training dataset
When the goal is live voice chat or real-time music continuation that must stream smoothly
When you are generating a fixed 30-second clip offline
Whenever you want to avoid using a vocoder
questions.explanation: The production note says users expect audio to arrive as it is generated, so tokens per second and streaming latency matter. Because flow-matching systems usually render fixed clips and need chunking plus overlap to stream, codec AR is the recommended path for real-time interactive products.
